title: Silver Alert: Why Investors Are Not Betting Against The Metal
speaker: Jeffrey Christian (CPM Group)

macro_themes.view: Fed raised 25bp last meeting; markets wrongly assume a pause because PCE flat; inflation (~3.4% headline, ~3% core) remains problematic.
Q2 GDP 2.2% driven by consumers borrowing on credit to make ends meet, a negative sign.
September payrolls only +29k, erratic jobs growth since COVID is worrisome.
VIX up but low historically; calm before a possible storm, though unclear the storm comes.
Uncertain economic/political environment should keep investors buying gold and silver; investment demand is the key price driver.

calls.reason: Downtrend since Jan record; H&S objective ~3,900 and trendline support 3,800-3,900 still possible, but secular bull market driven by investment demand expected to continue over coming quarters.
calls.quote: That's our view as to what's likely to happen over the next several months, if not several quarters, and on a longer term basis.

calls.reason: Testing $60 after 50% drop from $121 peak; market in surplus and ETP investors net sellers in 2026, needs large investor buying; positive that COMEX shorts remain very small.
calls.quote: It needs investors to be large net buyers of almost historical proportions to keep the silver price high and rising.

calls.reason: Palladium may be forming a base within $100 of current price after falling from ~$2,200, with some short-term weakness as gold/silver stay under pressure.
calls.quote: the palladium market probably will find a base, you know, within $100 of where it is today.

notes: Video recorded Fri 2 Oct 2026 11:50 NY. Gold view is two-sided: near-term downside risk to ~3,900 but secular bull intact (medium_term marked mixed). Palladium support 1067 derived from 'within $100' of 1167. Platinum mentioned only briefly (no clear call). PA not in canonical list; used PA.
